6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.DualNumberCarrierReduction
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.ChartTrivialityGeo
8	
9	/-!
10	# The two chart presentations at `ε ↦ 0` and the square between them (W5-T4, instantiation)
11	
12	`Tangent/ChartTrivialityGeo.lean` proves **(iii-c2-aff-geo)** over three hypotheses that it names
13	rather than builds: a presentation `e : Γ(Z, O) ≃+* A[ε]` upstairs, a presentation
14	`e' : Γ(X, g⁻¹O) ≃+* A` downstairs, and the square `hsq` intertwining `g.appLE` with `ε ↦ 0`. This
15	file supplies all three at the Wave-5 charts, with `Z = C_ε`, `X = C_k`, `A = Γ(C.left, W)` and
16	`g = relCurveMap C k[ε] k`:
17	
18	* `epsChartDown` — the downstairs presentation `Γ(C_k, fst⁻¹W) ≃+* Γ(C.left, W)`;
19	* `Over.dualNumberSectionsOfIsAffineOpen` (already landed) — the upstairs one, used through its
20	  `symm`;
21	* `relSectionsMap_eq_fstRingHom_comp` — **the square**.
22	
23	## Why the square was already three quarters written
24	
25	`Over.relSectionsMap_dualNumberSections` (`Tangent/DualNumberCarrierReduction.lean`) says
26	`relSectionsMap C k[ε] k W (dualNumberSections x) = sectionsBaseChange (fst x ⊗ₜ 1)`. That *is*
27	the square's content — the docstring there calls it "the statement the `ε`-kernel computation
28	spends". What was missing is only that its right-hand side is stated as a base-changed pure tensor
29	rather than as an element of `Γ(C.left, W)`; `Algebra.TensorProduct.rid` closes that gap, and
30	`epsChartDown` is precisely `sectionsBaseChange.symm` followed by `rid`.
31	
32	So the instantiation item that T4's residue had been reduced to is a *composition of landed
33	pieces*, and the honest reading is that (iii-c2-aff-geo) came with its own instantiation nearly
34	free. Recorded because the alternative reading — "the square is a new obligation" — is what the
35	roadmap said an hour before this file was written.
36	
37	## Two spelling notes, both of which cost a cycle
38	
39	**Both scoped instances must be opened.** `Over.sectionsAlgebra` is
40	`attribute [local instance]` (as in `DualNumberCarrier.lean`, `RelativeH1BaseChange.lean` and five
41	other files), and `TruncExpCech.EpsilonReduction`'s `epsAlgebra` is `scoped`. Without the first,
42	`Algebra k Γ(C.left, W)` fails to synthesize; without the second, `Algebra k[ε] k` does. Neither
43	absence means infrastructure is missing — the standing lesson of inbox `I-0567`/`I-0634`.
44	
45	**`sectionsBaseChangeOfIsAffineOpen` is `sectionsBaseChange` at the affine witness by `rfl`, but
46	`rw` will not see through it.** The proof therefore states that step as an explicit
47	`rw [show … from rfl]` before applying `RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply`. This is `I-0685`'s trap again:
48	the goal is type-correct and the message is about a spelling.
49	
50	## Scope
51	
52	`A` is instantiated at the *section ring of a chart*, not at `k` — which is why
53	`Tangent/EpsZeroSurjective.lean` was worth proving over an arbitrary commutative ring rather than
54	for `Spec k → Spec k[ε]`. The two files meet here.
55	
56	This file does **not** discharge `¬ IsAffine C.left` (the remaining input of
57	`Tangent/TwoChartHonest.lean`), and does not itself assemble the tangent-space conclusion: it
58	supplies the three chart-level hypotheses, at one affine open `W` at a time.
59	
60	## Main declarations
61	
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.epsChartDown` — the downstairs chart presentation.
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relSectionsMap_eq_fstRingHom_comp` — the square `hsq` of
64	  `Opens.cechPicMap_ι_eq_one_of_map_eq_one`.
65	
66	Reference: `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §§6.17, 6.27.
67	-/
68	
69	set_option autoImplicit false
70	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
71	
72	universe u
73	
74	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
75	open TensorProduct TruncExpCech DualNumber TrivSqZeroExt
76	
77	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
78	
79	open scoped TruncExpCech.EpsilonReduction
80	
81	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
82	
83	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
84	
85	/-- **The downstairs chart presentation.** Base-changing the curve along `k → k` does not change
86	its sections: `Γ(C_k, fst⁻¹W) ≃+* Γ(C.left, W)`, as `Over.sectionsBaseChange` (which presents the
87	left side as `Γ(C.left, W) ⊗[k] k`) followed by `Algebra.TensorProduct.rid`.
88	
89	This is the `e'` that `Opens.cechPicMap_ι_eq_one_of_map_eq_one` takes, at `A = Γ(C.left, W)`. -/
90	noncomputable def epsChartDown {W : C.left.Opens} (hW : IsAffineOpen W) :
91	    Γ(relCurve C k, (fst C (overSpec k k)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W) ≃+* Γ(C.left, W) :=
92	  (Over.sectionsBaseChangeOfIsAffineOpen C k hW).symm.trans
93	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.rid k k _).toRingEquiv
94	
95	/-- **The square `hsq`**: the relative-sections comparison along `ε ↦ 0`, read through the two
96	chart presentations, IS `ε ↦ 0` on dual numbers.
97	
98	`relSectionsMap C k[ε] k W` is by definition `(relCurveMap C k[ε] k).appLE` at the two chart
99	preimages (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean`), so this is exactly the hypothesis
100	`Opens.cechPicMap_ι_eq_one_of_map_eq_one` calls `hsq`, at
101	`g = relCurveMap C k[ε] k`, `A = Γ(C.left, W)`, `e = (dualNumberSectionsOfIsAffineOpen C hW).symm`
102	and `e' = epsChartDown C hW`.
103	
104	The content is `Over.relSectionsMap_dualNumberSections`; everything else is transporting its
105	right-hand side from a pure tensor to a section via `rid`. -/
106	theorem relSectionsMap_eq_fstRingHom_comp {W : C.left.Opens} (hW : IsAffineOpen W) :
107	    (epsChartDown C hW : Γ(relCurve C k, (fst C (overSpec k k)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W) →+* Γ(C.left, W)).comp
108	        (relSectionsMap C (DualNumber k) k W)
109	      = (TruncExpCech.fstRingHom (R := Γ(C.left, W))).comp
110	          ((Over.dualNumberSectionsOfIsAffineOpen C hW).symm :
111	            Γ((C ⊗ overSpec k (DualNumber k)).left,
112	              (fst C (overSpec k (DualNumber k))).left ⁻¹ᵁ W) →+* DualNumber Γ(C.left, W)) := by
113	  ext y
114	  simp only [RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]
115	  set x := (Over.dualNumberSectionsOfIsAffineOpen C hW).symm y with hx
116	  have hy : y = Over.dualNumberSectionsOfIsAffineOpen C hW x := by
117	    rw [hx, RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
118	  rw [hy]
119	  simp only [RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom]
120	  rw [Over.dualNumberSectionsOfIsAffineOpen, Over.relSectionsMap_dualNumberSections]
121	  change (Algebra.TensorProduct.rid k k _)
122	      ((Over.sectionsBaseChangeOfIsAffineOpen C k hW).symm
123	        ((Over.sectionsBaseChange C k hW.isCompact hW.isQuasiSeparated)
124	          (TrivSqZeroExt.fst x ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : k)))) = _
125	  rw [show (Over.sectionsBaseChange C k hW.isCompact hW.isQuasiSeparated)
126	        (TrivSqZeroExt.fst x ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : k))
127	      = (Over.sectionsBaseChangeOfIsAffineOpen C k hW)
128	          (TrivSqZeroExt.fst x ⊗ₜ[k] (1 : k)) from rfl,
129	    RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
130	  rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.rid_tmul, one_smul]
131	  change TrivSqZeroExt.fst x
132	      = fstRingHom ((Over.dualNumberSections C hW.isCompact hW.isQuasiSeparated).symm
133	          ((Over.dualNumberSections C hW.isCompact hW.isQuasiSeparated) x))
134	  rw [RingEquiv.symm_apply_apply, fstRingHom_apply]
135	
136	end AlgebraicGeometry

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TwoChartNaturality
7	
8	/-!
9	# Naturality of the DESCENDED two-chart comparison (W5-T4, intertwining item (1))
10	
11	`Tangent/TwoChartNaturality.lean` proves the reduction square for `twoChartClassHom` — the map
12	**before** the Čech quotient. The truncated-exponential engine of `Tangent/TruncExpCech.lean`
13	works between the quotients (`TruncExpCech.cechUnitsReduction`), so the square the kernel
14	computation consumes is the one for the descended `twoChartClass`. This file proves it.
15	
16	## Why the hom-level square was not enough (inbox `I-0630`)
17	
18	A fresh-context reviewer found that `map_twoChartClassHom`'s generality — no
19	`Function.Surjective sel`, no affineness — is a property of *that declaration*, and does not carry
20	to its consumer: `twoChartClass` exists only given `hsel`, so the quotient-level square needs
21	`hsel` at **both** ends (`sel` and `sel ∘ f.base`). Recorded as the standing rule at
22	`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §6.18: *a generality claim is scoped to the declaration it is written
23	on, not to the chain.*
24	
25	What was genuinely missing is one containment: that pulling back along `f` carries the Čech
26	coboundary subgroup of `Y` into that of `X`. Without it the pullback does not descend to the
27	quotients at all, so no square can be stated.
28	
29	## Implementation notes
30	
31	The containment (`cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsAppLE`) is **not** a cohomological statement.
32	A coboundary is `ρ₀ˣ(v₀) · ρ₁ˣ(v₁)` for chart units `vₛ : Γ(Y, V s)ˣ`, and the two `unitsAppLE`
33	functoriality lemmas already in the tree move the pullback past the restriction in both directions:
34	
35	* `Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE` — pullback after restriction, which retypes the generator as the
36	  pullback of the *chart* unit;
37	* `Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map` — restriction after pullback, which puts it back on the overlap.
38	
39	Both are `@[simp]`, so after `Scheme.resHom` is unfolded to `X.presheaf.map` — the spelling those
40	two lemmas are stated in — `simp` closes each factor. Unfolding `resHom` is what the proof actually
41	needs: with `resHom` folded, `rw` fails with *"the target expression is not type-correct under the
42	`instances` transparency level"*, the familiar symptom of the `Γ`/`presheaf.obj` coercion seam
43	recorded elsewhere in this directory. Neither `rfl` nor a hand-directed `rw` chain closes it; the
44	one-line `simp [Scheme.resHom]` does.
45	
46	The square itself is then free: `QuotientGroup.map_mk` and `twoChartClass_mk` reduce both sides to
47	the landed `map_twoChartClassHom`.
48	
49	## Main declarations
50	
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsAppLE` — the containment: pullback
52	  carries two-chart Čech coboundaries to coboundaries.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pullbackOverlapQuot` — the induced map of two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹`
54	  quotients.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.map_twoChartClass` — **the quotient-level reduction square**, the form
56	  the `ε`-kernel computation consumes.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.map_twoChartClass_eq_one_iff` — its kernel form.
58	
59	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5, proof of Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020);
60	`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §6.20(1).
61	-/
62	
63	set_option autoImplicit false
64	
65	universe u
66	
67	open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
68	
69	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
70	
71	namespace Scheme
72	
73	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {V : Bool → Y.Opens}
74	
75	/-! ## The containment: pullback carries Čech coboundaries to Čech coboundaries -/
76	
77	/-- **Pullback along `f` carries a two-chart Čech coboundary to a two-chart Čech coboundary.**
78	
79	A coboundary on `Y` is a product `ρ₀ˣ(v₀) · ρ₁ˣ(v₁)` of restrictions of *chart* units. Pulling
80	back commutes with restriction (`Hom.map_unitsAppLE`, then `Hom.unitsAppLE_map`), so the image is
81	the corresponding product of restrictions of the pulled-back chart units — a coboundary for the
82	preimage charts.
83	
84	This is the statement whose absence blocked the quotient-level square (inbox `I-0630`): without
85	it, `pullbackOverlapUnit` does not descend to the Čech `Ȟ¹` quotients. It is pure `unitsAppLE`
86	functoriality — no cocycles, no cohomology, no affineness, and no surjectivity of the selector. -/
87	theorem cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsAppLE (f : X ⟶ Y) :
88	    TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
89	        (Y.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
90	        (Y.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true)) ≤
91	      (TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
92	        (X.resHom (inf_le_left : f ⁻¹ᵁ V false ⊓ f ⁻¹ᵁ V true ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V false))
93	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : f ⁻¹ᵁ V false ⊓ f ⁻¹ᵁ V true ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V true))).comap
94	        (f.unitsAppLE (V false ⊓ V true) (f ⁻¹ᵁ V false ⊓ f ⁻¹ᵁ V true) le_rfl) := by
95	  intro u hu
96	  obtain ⟨v₀, v₁, rfl⟩ := TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
97	  refine Subgroup.mem_comap.mpr (TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mpr
98	    ⟨f.unitsAppLE (V false) (f ⁻¹ᵁ V false) le_rfl v₀,
99	      f.unitsAppLE (V true) (f ⁻¹ᵁ V true) le_rfl v₁, ?_⟩)
100	  rw [map_mul]
101	  congr 1 <;> simp [Scheme.resHom]
102	
103	/-! ## The induced map of Čech `Ȟ¹` quotients -/
104	
105	/-- **The pullback of two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹`-of-units classes** along `f`, i.e.
106	`pullbackOverlapUnit` descended to the quotients. Well defined by
107	`cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsAppLE`. -/
108	noncomputable def pullbackOverlapQuot (f : X ⟶ Y) :
109	    (Γ(Y, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ ⧸ TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
110	        (Y.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
111	        (Y.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))) →*
112	      (Γ(X, (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) false ⊓ (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) true)ˣ ⧸
113	        TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
114	          (X.resHom (inf_le_left : (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) false ⊓ (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) true
115	            ≤ (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) false))
116	          (X.resHom (inf_le_right : (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) false ⊓ (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) true
117	            ≤ (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) true))) :=
118	  QuotientGroup.map _ _ (f.unitsAppLE (V false ⊓ V true) (f ⁻¹ᵁ V false ⊓ f ⁻¹ᵁ V true) le_rfl)
119	    (cechCoboundaryUnits_le_comap_unitsAppLE f)
120	
121	@[simp]
122	theorem pullbackOverlapQuot_mk (f : X ⟶ Y) (u : Γ(Y, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) :
123	    pullbackOverlapQuot f (QuotientGroup.mk u)
124	      = QuotientGroup.mk (pullbackOverlapUnit f u) :=
125	  rfl
126	
127	/-! ## The quotient-level reduction square -/
128	
129	/-- **THE QUOTIENT-LEVEL REDUCTION SQUARE.** The descended comparison `twoChartClass` is natural
130	in the scheme: pulling back a two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹` class and then comparing to `CechPic` is
131	comparing and then pulling back.
132	
133	Unlike the hom-level `map_twoChartClassHom`, this needs `Function.Surjective sel` at **both** ends
134	— the source and the target of `twoChartClass` each exist only given it. That is exactly the
135	correction of inbox `I-0630`; see the module docstring.
136	
137	This is the square the `ε`-kernel computation consumes, because the truncated-exponential engine's
138	`TruncExpCech.cechUnitsReduction` is a map between these quotients, not between the unit groups. -/
139	theorem map_twoChartClass (f : X ⟶ Y) (sel : Y → Bool) (hmem : ∀ y, y ∈ V (sel y))
140	    (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
141	    (hsel' : Function.Surjective (fun x ↦ sel (f.base x)))
142	    (q : Γ(Y, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ ⧸ TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
143	      (Y.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
144	      (Y.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))) :
145	    Scheme.CechPic.map f (twoChartClass V sel hmem hsel q)
146	      = twoChartClass (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) (fun x ↦ sel (f.base x))
147	          (fun x ↦ hmem (f.base x)) hsel' (pullbackOverlapQuot f q) := by
148	  induction q using QuotientGroup.induction_on with
149	  | H u =>
150	    rw [twoChartClass_mk, pullbackOverlapQuot_mk, twoChartClass_mk, map_twoChartClassHom]
151	
152	/-- **The kernel form of the quotient-level square**: a two-chart Čech class dies in `X.CechPic`
153	after pullback exactly when its pulled-back class does. This is the shape the `ε`-kernel
154	computation reads, since `twoChartClass` is injective (`twoChartClass_injective`) and so the
155	`CechPic`-level kernel is computed by the `Ȟ¹`-level one. -/
156	theorem map_twoChartClass_eq_one_iff (f : X ⟶ Y) (sel : Y → Bool) (hmem : ∀ y, y ∈ V (sel y))
157	    (hsel : Function.Surjective sel)
158	    (hsel' : Function.Surjective (fun x ↦ sel (f.base x)))
159	    (q : Γ(Y, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ ⧸ TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
160	      (Y.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
161	      (Y.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))) :
162	    Scheme.CechPic.map f (twoChartClass V sel hmem hsel q) = 1
163	      ↔ pullbackOverlapQuot f q = 1 := by
164	  rw [map_twoChartClass f sel hmem hsel hsel' q]
165	  constructor
166	  · intro h
167	    exact (injective_iff_map_eq_one _).mp
168	      (twoChartClass_injective (fun s ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ V s) (fun x ↦ sel (f.base x))
169	        (fun x ↦ hmem (f.base x)) hsel') _ h
170	  · intro h
171	    rw [h, map_one]
172	
173	end Scheme
174	
175	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.DualNumberCarrier
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.TruncExpCech
8	
9	/-!
10	# The carrier translation matches the two Čech coboundary subgroups (W5-T4, item (2))
11	
12	`Tangent/DualNumberCarrier.lean` builds the carrier translation
13	`Γ(C, W)[ε] ≃+* Γ(C_ε, fst⁻¹ W)` and proves it natural in the open. That makes the two Čech `Ȟ¹`
14	*carriers* isomorphic — and, as inbox `I-0571` records and `I-0630` re-found in this file's
15	neighbour, an isomorphism of the two ends of a map says nothing about the map, while the Wave-5
16	computation is a **kernel**. This file closes that gap on the coboundary side:
17	
18	```
19	Subgroup.map (dualNumberSectionsUnits C) (cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom res₀) (mapRingHom res₁))
20	  = cechCoboundaryUnits res₀' res₁'
21	```
22	
23	(`Over.map_cechCoboundaryUnits_dualNumberSectionsUnits`), where the primed restrictions are those of
24	the **thickened** charts. With that equality the translation descends to a `MulEquiv` of the two
25	two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹`-of-units groups (`Over.dualNumberCechH1Equiv`) — the object the `ε`-kernel
26	computation consumes, rather than the two carriers at its ends.
27	
28	## Why an equality and not a containment
29	
30	A containment would let the map descend but would not identify the quotients: the descended map
31	could have a kernel arising from the target subgroup being strictly larger. Since both inclusions
32	come from the *same* square applied to the equivalence and to its inverse, the equality costs one
33	extra `le_antisymm` branch — and settling for `≤` would leave exactly the gap `I-0630`(2) named
34	("the two `H¹` carriers are still only abstractly isomorphic").
35	
36	## Implementation notes
37	
38	`cechCoboundaryUnits` is a join of two `MonoidHom.range`s, and `Subgroup.map` distributes over `⊔`
39	(`Subgroup.map_sup`, `MonoidHom.map_range`), so the whole statement reduces to **one range
40	identification per chart** and no case analysis on `Bool` ever appears. Each range identification is
41	`Over.unitsMap_resHom_dualNumberSectionsUnits` — the landed naturality-in-the-open square — read
42	forwards for `≤` and applied to the preimage of a thickened chart unit (via
43	`MulEquiv.apply_symm_apply`) for `≥`.
44	
45	**One spelling trap, measured.** `Over.unitsMap_resHom_dualNumberSectionsUnits` is stated with
46	`Over.resAlgHom C h` coerced to a `RingHom`, whereas `cechCoboundaryUnits` at the two-chart datum is
47	stated with `C.left.resHom h`. The two are equal by `rfl`, and `exact` accepts either — but `rw`
48	cannot see through the coercion, failing with *"the target expression is not type-correct under the
49	`instances` transparency level"*. So `range_dualNumberSectionsUnits_comp` is **stated in the
50	`resHom` spelling** (the consumer's), not the `resAlgHom` one; with that choice the subgroup
51	equality is a single `rw` chain. Same family as the seam recorded in
52	`Tangent/TwoChartQuotientNaturality.lean`.
53	
54	## Main declarations
55	
56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.range_dualNumberSectionsUnits_comp` — the per-chart range identification.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.map_cechCoboundaryUnits_dualNumberSectionsUnits` — **item (2)**: the
58	  translation carries the thickened coboundary subgroup **onto** the base one.
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.dualNumberCechH1Equiv` — the induced isomorphism of two-chart Čech
60	  `Ȟ¹`-of-units groups, with `dualNumberCechH1Equiv_mk`.
61	
62	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5 Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020);
63	`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §6.20(2).
64	-/

97	    (hW : IsCompact ((W : Set C.left))) (hW' : IsQuasiSeparated ((W : Set C.left)))
98	    (h : W ≤ V) :

104	            (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono

110	  · rintro x ⟨v, rfl⟩

112	    have := Over.unitsMap_resHom_dualNumberSectionsUnits C hV hV' hW hW' h
113	      ((Over.dualNumberSectionsUnits C hV hV').symm v)
114	    rw [MulEquiv.apply_symm_apply] at this

119	equivalence of the two Čech `Ȟ¹` **quotients**, and it is what inbox `I-0630`(2) found missing:
120	`resHom_dualNumberSections` made it provable, but nobody had proved it, so the two `H¹` groups were
121	only abstractly isomorphic — worthless to a kernel computation (`I-0571`).
122	
123	Proof: `Subgroup.map` distributes over the join `cechCoboundaryUnits` is built from, leaving one
124	range identification per chart (`range_dualNumberSectionsUnits_comp`). No dual-number algebra, no
125	case split. -/
126	theorem map_cechCoboundaryUnits_dualNumberSectionsUnits {V : Bool → C.left.Opens}
127	    (hc : ∀ s, IsCompact ((V s : Set C.left))) (hq : ∀ s, IsQuasiSeparated ((V s : Set C.left)))
128	    (hci : IsCompact (((V false ⊓ V true : C.left.Opens) : Set C.left)))
129	    (hqi : IsQuasiSeparated (((V false ⊓ V true : C.left.Opens) : Set C.left))) :
130	    Subgroup.map (Over.dualNumberSectionsUnits C hci hqi).toMonoidHom
131	        (cechCoboundaryUnits
132	          (mapRingHom (C.left.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false)))
133	          (mapRingHom (C.left.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))))
134	      = cechCoboundaryUnits
135	          ((C ⊗ overSpec k (DualNumber k)).left.resHom
136	            (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k (DualNumber k))).left
137	              (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false)))
138	          ((C ⊗ overSpec k (DualNumber k)).left.resHom
139	            (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k (DualNumber k))).left
140	              (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))) := by
141	  rw [cechCoboundaryUnits, cechCoboundaryUnits, Subgroup.map_sup, MonoidHom.map_range,
142	    MonoidHom.map_range,
143	    range_dualNumberSectionsUnits_comp C (hc false) (hq false) hci hqi inf_le_left,
144	    range_dualNumberSectionsUnits_comp C (hc true) (hq true) hci hqi inf_le_right]
145	
146	/-- **The two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹`-of-units groups agree across the carrier translation.** The
147	truncated-exponential engine of `Tangent/TruncExpCech.lean` computes with the left-hand quotient
148	(`DualNumber` of the *original* overlap sections); the two-chart comparison
149	`Scheme.twoChartClass` consumes the right-hand one (units of the *thickened* overlap sections). This
150	is the isomorphism between them, at quotient level.
151	
152	`QuotientGroup.congr` of the carrier translation and the subgroup equality above. Because it is
153	built from that equality rather than asserted, a consumer may transport a **kernel** across it —
154	which the carrier equivalence alone did not license. -/
155	noncomputable def dualNumberCechH1Equiv {V : Bool → C.left.Opens}
156	    (hc : ∀ s, IsCompact ((V s : Set C.left))) (hq : ∀ s, IsQuasiSeparated ((V s : Set C.left)))
157	    (hci : IsCompact (((V false ⊓ V true : C.left.Opens) : Set C.left)))
158	    (hqi : IsQuasiSeparated (((V false ⊓ V true : C.left.Opens) : Set C.left))) :
159	    ((DualNumber Γ(C.left, V false ⊓ V true))ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits
160	        (mapRingHom (C.left.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false)))
161	        (mapRingHom (C.left.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true)))) ≃*
162	      (Γ((C ⊗ overSpec k (DualNumber k)).left,
163	          (fst C (overSpec k (DualNumber k))).left ⁻¹ᵁ (V false ⊓ V true))ˣ ⧸
164	        cechCoboundaryUnits
165	          ((C ⊗ overSpec k (DualNumber k)).left.resHom
166	            (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k (DualNumber k))).left
167	              (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false)))
168	          ((C ⊗ overSpec k (DualNumber k)).left.resHom
169	            (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k (DualNumber k))).left
170	              (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true)))) :=
171	  QuotientGroup.congr _ _ (Over.dualNumberSectionsUnits C hci hqi)
172	    (map_cechCoboundaryUnits_dualNumberSectionsUnits C hc hq hci hqi)

==== 6.26 worksheet
### 6.26 (3c) IS CLOSED — the seam is an ISO, and the only obstacle was a spelling

*Run 0073 r5, `Tangent/DualNumberUnitTransport.lean`, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 with zero diagnostics.
Written after the Lean this once and saying so: §6.23 had already done the worksheet-first work —
it named the obligation, diagnosed it to the exact step, and prescribed a route. What follows
records where that prescription was right, where it over-priced, and where it under-priced.*

**THE STATEMENT.** With `unitIso k : Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k)) ≅ overSpec k k`:

```
overDualNumberZero k = (unitIso k).hom ≫ overSpecMap k[ε] k          -- overDualNumberZero_eq
(C ◁ overDualNumberZero k).left = transportLeft C ≫ relCurveMap C k[ε] k
                                                     -- whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero_left
IsIso (transportLeft C)                                     -- isIso_transportLeft
```

The second is *exactly* the identification §6.24 isolated as **"the step that turns two aligned
diagrams into one commuting one"** — the engine's arrow reaches the base through `relCurveMap`,
item (1)'s reaches it through the `ε ↦ 0` scheme morphism, and this is the equation between them.

**WHERE §6.23's PRESCRIPTION OVER-PRICED.** It said *"`eqToHom`/`Over.isoMk` along `Spec.map_id`,
then a whiskering congruence"*. **The `eqToHom` half is never needed.** The two source objects have
the *same underlying scheme* `Spec k` — that much **is** `rfl`, and `Over.isoMk (Iso.refl _)` takes
the left component. `Spec.map_id` is spent on one thing only: the structure-morphism triangle
`𝟙 ≫ Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k)) = 𝟙`. And the whiskering congruence is `whiskerLeft_comp`
plus the landed **(3b)** reversed. Total: three short lemmas.

Worth naming because it is the *mirror* of this lane's usual error. The habitual failure is
under-pricing (a claimed `rfl` that isn't). Here the retraction that corrected an under-pricing
went on to over-price the repair — a diagnosis reached under the sting of being wrong reached for
the heaviest available tool. **A retraction is not automatically a correct re-estimate.**

**WHERE IT UNDER-PRICED, AND THIS IS THE USEFUL HALF.** §6.23 described (3c) as *a transport*, which
suggests a one-directional rewrite. It is an **isomorphism** (`isIso_transportLeft`): whiskering an
iso is an iso, and `Over.forget` carries that to schemes. So a consumer may travel the seam in
**either** direction — and a kernel comparison *must*, since "dies after pullback ⟺ dies before" is
a two-way statement. An `eqToHom`-shaped mental model would have obtained the forward rewrite and
left the reverse looking like new work.

**THE ONE REAL OBSTACLE, and it was not mathematics.** The composite with `relCurveMap` is
`rfl`-equal to the whiskering spelling, but `rw` refuses it:

```
Application type mismatch: relCurveMap C k[ε] k has type relCurve C k ⟶ relCurve C k[ε]
  but is expected to have type (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left ⟶ relCurve C k[ε]
Note: The target expression is not type-correct under the `instances` transparency level
```

`(C ⊗ overSpec k k).left = relCurve C k` **is** `rfl` (measured), so the goal is type-correct and
that message names a *spelling*, not a defect — inbox `I-0685`'s trap, met here for the first time
in this lane. Fixed by giving the transport a **definition whose declared type already ends in
`relCurve C k`**; both spellings then coexist, `_left'` (whiskering) proving `_left` (relCurveMap)
by term with no transport at all.

> **Rule, and it is the (3b)/(3c) pair read together.** §6.22's rule was *unfold to the `RingHom`
> and try `rfl` at every level*. Add: **when `rw` reports a type mismatch on terms you believe are
> `rfl`-equal, test that belief with `example : lhsType = rhsType := rfl` before concluding the goal
> is malformed.** Two `rfl` outcomes with opposite meanings live one line apart here — the objects
> `overSpec k k` vs the unit are genuinely **not** defeq (that is (3c)), while the *carriers*
> `(C ⊗ overSpec k k).left` vs `relCurve C k` **are** (that is the spelling). Confusing the two costs
> either a false claim or an invented obstacle.

theorem isAffine_of_V₀_eq_bot (h : D.V₀ = ⊥) : IsAffine Y := by
  have hv1 : D.V₁ = ⊤ := by
    have hs := D.sup_eq_top
    rw [h, bot_sup_eq] at hs

/-- **The selector of a two-chart cover of a NON-AFFINE scheme is surjective** — the `hsel` binder
of `Scheme.map_twoChartClass`, from one hypothesis about the ambient scheme rather than two about
the first chart.

`surjective_selector_iff` asks for `V₀ ≠ ⊥ ∧ V₀ ≠ ⊤`; both degeneracies make `Y` affine
(`isAffine_of_V₀_eq_bot`, `isAffine_of_V₀_eq_top`), so `¬ IsAffine Y` supplies both at once. No
non-emptiness hypothesis is needed: the empty scheme is affine, hence already excluded. -/

variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]

/-- **The kernel of `ε ↦ 0` consists of nilpotents.** `ker fstRingHom = (ε)` (`ker_fstRingHom`) and
`ε² = 0`, so the generator is nilpotent of order 2 and `Ideal.span_le` finishes. -/
theorem ker_fstRingHom_le_nilradical :
    RingHom.ker (fstRingHom (R := A)) ≤ nilradical (DualNumber A) := by
  rw [ker_fstRingHom, Ideal.span_le, Set.singleton_subset_iff]
  exact ⟨2, by simp⟩

/-- **`Spec` of `ε ↦ 0` is a homeomorphism** — the thickened affine line has exactly the points of
the line it thickens.

`PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap` needs two inputs: every element of the source ring has a power in
the range (here `n = 1`, since `fst` is surjective) and the kernel is contained in the nilradical
(`ker_fstRingHom_le_nilradical`). Both are cheap because `ε` is nilpotent, and neither needs `A` to
be a field. -/
theorem isHomeomorph_comap_fstRingHom :
    IsHomeomorph (PrimeSpectrum.comap (fstRingHom (R := A))) :=
  PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap _
    (fun x => ⟨1, by simpa using fstRingHom_surjective x⟩) ker_fstRingHom_le_nilradical

/-- **The binder `Tangent/TwoChartSelector.lean` names**: `Spec.map (ε ↦ 0)` is surjective on
points, so `Scheme.surjective_selector_comp` applies at the `ε ↦ 0` morphism and
`Scheme.map_twoChartClass`'s second surjectivity hypothesis `hsel'` has a producer.

`Spec.map`'s underlying map **is** `PrimeSpectrum.comap` definitionally, so this is
`isHomeomorph_comap_fstRingHom.surjective` by `exact` — `simpa` actually *fails* here, having
rewritten the goal into a shape where the two carriers no longer match. (One more instance of
`I-0685`: when a term should apply directly, try it before normalising.) -/
theorem specMap_fstRingHom_base_surjective :
    Function.Surjective
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (fstRingHom (R := A)))).base :=
  isHomeomorph_comap_fstRingHom.surjective

consumer supplies them.

**And "both hold for the curve" is at present an argument, not a witness in this project** — the
distinction inbox `I-0679` names (a hypothesis can be satisfiable and yet witnessed nowhere, which
every ordinary check reports as healthy). Measured: `Scheme.AffineTwoCover.nonempty_of_curve`
supplies a cover of the curve but says nothing about either chart being proper or non-empty, and a
search of both projects and mathlib finds no declaration concluding `V₀ ≠ ⊥` or `V₀ ≠ ⊤` for it. So a
consumer instantiating this lemma at the Wave-5 curve **must still produce those two facts**, and
should not expect to find them lying about. Recorded rather than papered over. -/
theorem surjective_selector_iff :
    Function.Surjective D.selector ↔ D.V₀ ≠ ⊥ ∧ D.V₀ ≠ ⊤ := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro hs
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hs false
      rw [selector] at hx
      have hxV : x ∈ D.V₀ := by by_contra h; simp [h] at hx
      intro hbot
      rw [hbot] at hxV
      exact hxV
    · obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hs true
      rw [selector] at hx
      have hxV : x ∉ D.V₀ := by by_contra h; simp [h] at hx
      intro htop
      exact hxV (htop ▸ trivial)
  · rintro ⟨h0, h1⟩ s
    cases s
    · obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, x ∈ D.V₀ := by
        by_contra hc
        simp only [not_exists] at hc
        exact h0 (by ext x; simpa using hc x)
      exact ⟨x, by rw [selector, if_pos hx]⟩
    · obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, x ∉ D.V₀ := by
        by_contra hc
        simp only [not_exists, not_not] at hc
        exact h1 (by ext x; simpa using hc x)
      exact ⟨x, by rw [selector, if_neg hx]⟩

end AffineTwoCover

/-! ## The SECOND surjectivity binder, and a producer for it

`Scheme.map_twoChartClass` (`Tangent/TwoChartQuotientNaturality.lean`) takes **two** surjectivity
hypotheses — `hsel` for the selector on `Y` and `hsel'` for `sel ∘ f.base` on `X`. A reviewer
(inbox `I-0688`) found that the second had **no producer anywhere in the project**: grepping `hsel'`
returns only occurrences inside the declaration itself, so every consumer would have had to invent
it. That is an obligation *moved*, not discharged, and a carrier-level "level check" cannot see it
because binders do not appear in carriers.

The lemma below is the producer. It is deliberately stated as the general composition fact rather
than at `f = ε ↦ 0`, because that is where the content is: **surjectivity of the selector at the
pulled-back end follows from surjectivity at the base end together with surjectivity of `f.base`.**
So a consumer owes a topological fact about `f`, not a new combinatorial one about charts.

For the Wave-5 instance `f = ` the `ε ↦ 0` map `C ⟶ C_ε`, `f.base` is surjective — it is a
homeomorphism on points, `Spec k → Spec k[ε]` being a bijection of one-point spaces (the standing
observation of `Tangent/RelPicPointTest.lean`). That last step is **not** proved here; it is named as
what the consumer supplies, in the same spirit as `V₀ ≠ ⊥`/`V₀ ≠ ⊤` above. -/
theorem Scheme.surjective_selector_comp {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (sel : Y → Bool)
    (hsel : Function.Surjective sel) (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) :
    Function.Surjective (fun x ↦ sel (f.base x)) :=
  hsel.comp hf

18	Worksheet §6.23 recorded that retraction and named the residue: *an object transport along
19	`Spec.map_id`, then a whiskering congruence.* This file builds it.
20	
21	## The finding: the transport is an ISO, not an `eqToHom`, and the factorisation is one `rw`
22	
23	The predecessor's diagnosis prescribed `eqToHom`/`Over.isoMk` along `Spec.map_id`. Measured, the
24	`Over.isoMk` half is the whole story and the `eqToHom` half is never needed:
25	
26	* `unitIso k : Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k)) ≅ overSpec k k` is `Over.isoMk (Iso.refl _)` — the two objects
27	  have the *same* underlying scheme `Spec k` (that much **is** `rfl`); only the two structure
28	  morphisms to `Spec k` differ, and `specMap_algebraMap_self_eq_id` is exactly the triangle.
29	* `overDualNumberZero k = (unitIso k).hom ≫ overSpecMap k[ε] k` (`overDualNumberZero_eq`) —
30	  after `Over.OverMorphism.ext` and `Category.id_comp` this is the landed **(3b)** lemma
31	  `overSpecMap_eps_eq_overDualNumberZero`, reversed.
32	* Whiskering is functorial, so the same factorisation holds after `C ◁ -` and after `.left`
33	  (`whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero`, `whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero_left`) — and the second factor
34	  of the `.left` form is `relCurveMap C k[ε] k` **on the nose**, which is the identification
35	  worksheet §6.24 called "the step that turns two aligned diagrams into one commuting one".
36	
37	**So (3c) is a transport by an isomorphism**: `transportLeft C` below is an `IsIso`
38	(`isIso_transportLeft`), whiskering an iso being an iso and `Over.forget` preserving that. A
39	consumer therefore does not merely *rewrite* along the seam, it may **invert** it — which is what a
40	kernel comparison needs, since an injectivity/kernel statement must travel in both directions.
41	
42	## Why this needed a named definition rather than a `rw` at the use site
43	
44	`(C ◁ (unitIso k).hom).left` and `transportLeft C` are the same term, but the *spelling* decides
45	whether the composite with `relCurveMap` elaborates: written inline, Lean assigns the composite's
46	left factor a type ending in `(C ⊗ overSpec k k).left`, and `relCurveMap C k[ε] k` is typed
47	`relCurve C k ⟶ relCurve C k[ε]`. Those unfold to the same scheme, so the goal *is* type-correct,
48	but `rw` reports
49	
50	```
51	Application type mismatch … but is expected to have type
52	  (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left ⟶ relCurve C k[ε]
53	Note: The target expression is not type-correct under the `instances` transparency level
54	```
55	
56	which reads like a broken goal and is not one (inbox `I-0685`: *rfl-equal spellings block `rw`*).
57	Giving the transport a definition whose **declared type** already says `⟶ relCurve C k` fixes the
58	spelling once, and `whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero_left` then typechecks as a restatement of the
59	whiskering form — proof term `whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero_left'`, no transport, no `eqToHom`.
60	
61	## Main declarations
62	
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.unitIso` — the source-object seam, `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k)) ≅ overSpec k k`.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.overDualNumberZero_eq` — **(3c) at the test-object level**: `ε ↦ 0` factors as
65	  the seam followed by the coefficient comparison.
66	* `AlgebraicGeometry.whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero` / `..._left` / `..._left'` — the same after
67	  `C ◁ -`, and after `.left` in both spellings.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.transportLeft` — the seam on relative curves,
69	  `(C ⊗ Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))).left ⟶ relCurve C k`, with `isIso_transportLeft`.
70	
71	Reference: `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §§6.20(3), 6.23, 6.24, 6.26.
72	-/

74	set_option autoImplicit false
75	
76	universe u
77	
78	open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
79	
80	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
81	
82	open TruncExpCech.EpsilonReduction DualNumber
83	
84	variable (k : Type u) [Field k]
85	
86	/-! ## The source-object seam -/
87	
88	/-- **The monoidal unit of `Over (Spec k)` is `overSpec k k`, as an isomorphism.**
89	
90	The two objects have the *same* underlying scheme `Spec k` — that is `rfl`, and is why
91	`Iso.refl` suffices for the left component. What is not `rfl`, and is the entire content of
92	worksheet §6.23's retraction, is that their structure morphisms agree: `Spec.map` of the identity
93	algebra map is the identity only *propositionally*
94	(`specMap_algebraMap_self_eq_id`, i.e. `Spec.map_id`). -/
95	noncomputable def unitIso : Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≅ overSpec k k :=
96	  Over.isoMk (Iso.refl _) (by
97	    change 𝟙 _ ≫ (overSpec k k).hom = (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).hom
98	    rw [Category.id_comp]
99	    exact specMap_algebraMap_self_eq_id k)
100	
101	@[simp]
102	theorem unitIso_hom_left : (unitIso k).hom.left = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) := rfl
103	
104	/-! ## (3c): the factorisation -/
105	
106	/-- **(3c), at the test-object level.** The `ε ↦ 0` morphism out of the monoidal unit factors as
107	the source-object seam followed by the coefficient comparison `overSpecMap k[ε] k`.
108	
109	This is the object transport worksheet §6.23 named as T4's residue after retracting the claim that
110	it was free. It is *not* free — `unitIso` is where `Spec.map_id` is spent — but it is one lemma, and
111	once the seam is applied the remaining equation is exactly the landed **(3b)**
112	`overSpecMap_eps_eq_overDualNumberZero`. -/
113	theorem overDualNumberZero_eq :
114	    overDualNumberZero k = (unitIso k).hom ≫ overSpecMap (k := k) (DualNumber k) k := by
115	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
116	  change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TruncExpCech.fstRingHom (R := k)))
117	      = (unitIso k).hom.left ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (DualNumber k) k))
118	  change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TruncExpCech.fstRingHom (R := k)))
119	      = 𝟙 _ ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (DualNumber k) k))
120	  rw [Category.id_comp]
121	  exact (overSpecMap_eps_eq_overDualNumberZero k).symm
122	
123	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
124	
125	/-- The factorisation after whiskering with the curve — `C ◁ -` is a functor, so this is
126	`overDualNumberZero_eq` transported by `whiskerLeft_comp`. -/
127	theorem whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero :
128	    (C ◁ overDualNumberZero k)
129	      = (C ◁ (unitIso k).hom) ≫ (C ◁ overSpecMap (k := k) (DualNumber k) k) := by
130	  rw [← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp, ← overDualNumberZero_eq]
131	  rfl
132	
133	/-- The factorisation on the underlying schemes, in the whiskering spelling. -/
134	theorem whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero_left' :
135	    (C ◁ overDualNumberZero k).left
136	      = (C ◁ (unitIso k).hom).left ≫ (C ◁ overSpecMap (k := k) (DualNumber k) k).left := by
137	  rw [← Over.comp_left, ← whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero]
138	
139	/-! ## The transport on relative curves -/
140	
141	/-- **The (3c) seam on relative curves.** The same morphism as `(C ◁ (unitIso k).hom).left`, but
142	with its *declared* type ending in `relCurve C k` — which is what lets a composite with
143	`relCurveMap` elaborate. See the module docstring: the inline spelling is `rfl`-equal but blocks
144	`rw` under `instances` transparency. -/
145	noncomputable def transportLeft :
146	    (C ⊗ Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).left ⟶ relCurve C k :=
147	  (C ◁ (unitIso k).hom).left
148	
149	/-- **(3c) in the form the tangent computation reads**: the `ε ↦ 0` map of relative curves is the
150	seam followed by `relCurveMap C k[ε] k`.
151	
152	This is the identification worksheet §6.24 isolated as the one missing link between the two aligned
153	diagrams — the engine's arrow (`unitsFst` on the dual-number carrier, reached through
154	`relCurveMap`) and item (1)'s arrow (`pullbackOverlapQuot` along the `ε ↦ 0` scheme morphism). -/
155	theorem whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero_left :
156	    (C ◁ overDualNumberZero k).left
157	      = transportLeft k C ≫ relCurveMap C (DualNumber k) k :=
158	  whiskerLeft_overDualNumberZero_left' k C
159	
160	/-- **The seam is invertible.** `unitIso` is an isomorphism, `C ◁ -` preserves isomorphisms, and
161	`Over.forget` carries the result to schemes. So a consumer may transport a kernel or injectivity
162	statement across the seam in *either* direction — which is what a kernel comparison needs, and what
163	an `eqToHom`-only diagnosis would not have made obvious. -/
164	instance isIso_transportLeft : IsIso (transportLeft k C) := by
165	  have h : IsIso (C ◁ (unitIso k).hom) :=
166	    inferInstanceAs (IsIso (whiskerLeftIso C (unitIso k)).hom)
167	  exact inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((Over.forget _).map (C ◁ (unitIso k).hom)))
168

### 6.24 THE LEVEL CHECK, RUN EXPLICITLY: do items (1)+(2) actually meet the engine?

*Run 0073 r4. §6.18's rule says a generality or closure claim must be checked at its CONSUMER, and
this lane has broken that rule four times in a day. So rather than assert that items (1) and (2)
"compose with the T2 engine", here is the carrier-by-carrier comparison, read off the declarations.*

**The engine** (`TwoCover.unitsReduction`, `Tangent/TruncExpCechH1.lean:133`) is

```
(Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)[ε])ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (mapRingHom (X.resHom inf_le_left))
                                          (mapRingHom (X.resHom inf_le_right))
  →*  Γ(X, U₀ ⊓ U₁)ˣ ⧸ cechCoboundaryUnits (X.resHom inf_le_left) (X.resHom inf_le_right)
```

**The comparison** (`Scheme.twoChartClass`, `Tangent/TwoChartCechPic.lean`) has source

```
Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ ⧸ TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits (X.resHom inf_le_left)
                                                          (X.resHom inf_le_right)
```

**Verdict, and it is favourable.** The engine's **target** is *syntactically* the comparison's
source at `X` (same carrier, same subgroup, same two restriction maps). The engine's **source** is
the `DualNumber`-of-original-sections carrier, which is precisely what item (2)'s
`dualNumberCechH1Equiv` identifies with the comparison's source at the *thickened* curve. And item
(1)'s `map_twoChartClass` is the square for the induced map between the two comparison sources. So
the three pieces do line up at one level, which is what §6.18 said had to be checked and not
assumed.

**What is therefore still missing is exactly one link, stated sharply.** The engine's arrow is
`unitsFst` on the dual-number carrier; item (1)'s arrow is `pullbackOverlapQuot` along the `ε ↦ 0`
scheme morphism. Saying these are *the same arrow* across `dualNumberCechH1Equiv` is precisely
`(b-coeff)` composed with the (3c) object transport — which is why (3c) is not cosmetic bookkeeping:
**it is the step that turns two aligned diagrams into one commuting one.** Recorded here so no
successor reads §§6.21–6.22 as "the intertwining is done".

So the residue of §6.23 stands unchanged and is now justified rather than asserted: **(3c)** and
**(iii-c2-aff-geo)**.

### 6.25 REVIEWER FINDINGS ACCEPTED: a level check does not see BINDERS, and a retraction must reach the docstrings

*Fresh-context reviewer, inbox `I-0687` and `I-0688`. Both accepted in full; both point at the same
weakness from different sides, and one of them is a genuinely new failure mode for this lane.*

**`I-0688`, and it is the sharper of the two. §6.24's level check passed while an obligation was
being MOVED rather than discharged.** `Scheme.map_twoChartClass` takes **two** surjectivity binders:
`hsel` for `sel` on `Y`, and `hsel'` for `sel ∘ f.base` on `X`. I characterized the first
(`surjective_selector_iff`) and never asked who produces the second. Measured on the reviewer's
instruction: `grep -rn "hsel'"` returns **only occurrences inside my own declaration** — zero
producers anywhere in the project. A carrier-by-carrier comparison cannot detect this, because
**binders do not appear in carriers**.

> **Rule: "does this meet its consumer" is TWO passes, not one.** (1) do the carriers/types line up;
> (2) does every explicit hypothesis binder of the new lemma have a **producer** in the tree — grep
> the binder's statement and count occurrences *outside* the declaration itself. Zero means the
> consumer must invent it. Pass 2 is one grep, and it is the pass that catches an obligation being
> relocated rather than discharged. Corollary the reviewer states and I endorse: **characterizing
> one of two binders does not size the residue.**

**Acted on, not merely recorded.** `Tangent/TwoChartSelector.lean` now carries
`Scheme.surjective_selector_comp`: `hsel` plus `Function.Surjective f.base` gives `hsel'`. Stated as
the general composition fact on purpose — it relocates the obligation from a *combinatorial* fact
about charts to a *topological* fact about `f`, which is where it belongs and where the Wave-5
instance can discharge it (the `ε ↦ 0` map is a bijection on points, `Spec k → Spec k[ε]` being a map
of one-point spaces). That last step is named, not proved, exactly like `V₀ ≠ ⊥`/`V₀ ≠ ⊤`.

**`I-0687`: my §6.23 retraction did not reach the docstring of the theorem it was about.** The
sentence *"the source objects agree for the same reason: `overSpec k k` is
`Over.mk (Spec.map (ofHom (algebraMap k k)))` and `algebraMap k k = RingHom.id k`"* survived,
unstruck, in `overSpecMap_eps_eq_overDualNumberZero`'s docstring — **two declarations above the
theorem that refutes it.** So a reader of that docstring alone got the withdrawn claim with no
marker. Fixed in place: the docstring now says the lemma is about the two *morphisms only*, names the
sentence as withdrawn with its inbox reference, and points at
`specMap_algebraMap_self_eq_id`. Two stale worksheet lines ("nothing else stands between…", §§6.21
and 6.22) are struck likewise.

**This is "retract where the claim is" recurring in the file that records the lesson**, which is the
second time today, and the reason is worth naming: I struck the *worksheet* prose and treated the
Lean docstrings as a separate artifact. They are not — **a docstring is the copy a consumer actually
reads.** When retracting, grep the retracted sentence across `.lean` files too, not only the notes.

transport~~ (**CLOSED, §6.26**), **(iii-c2-aff-geo)**, and — newly explicit — the two named consumer

data.content:
simp [TrivSqZeroExt.algebraMap_eq_inl]
  rw [← Spec.map_comp, h, Spec.map_id]

/-- **The dual-number test object** `Spec k[ε]` as an object of `Over (Spec k)`.
Its pointed `X`-valued points at a section `e` of a `k`-scheme `X` form the
Zariski tangent space `T_e X` (Mumford, "Abelian varieties", §II.4). -/
noncomputable def overDualNumber (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
  Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (DualNumber k))))

/-- **The `ε ↦ 0` point** `Spec k ⟶ Spec k[ε]`, as a morphism in
`Over (Spec k)` out of the trivial over-object. Restricting a tangent vector
along it recovers the underlying point. -/
noncomputable def overDualNumberZero (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ⟶ overDualNumber k :=
  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (TruncExpCech.fstRingHom (R := k))))
    (specMap_fstRingHom_comp k)

/-- **The augmentation** `Spec k[ε] ⟶ Spec k`, as a morphism in `Over (Spec k)`
into the trivial over-object. Composition with it produces the "constant"
tangent vectors. -/
noncomputable def overDualNumberAugment (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    overDualNumber k ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
  Over.homMk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (DualNumber k))))
    (Category.comp_id _)

/-- The `ε ↦ 0` point and the augmentation form a retract pair. -/
lemma overDualNumberZero_comp_augment (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    overDualNumberZero k ≫ overDualNumberAugment k
      = 𝟙 (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))) := by
  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
  exact specMap_fstRingHom_comp k

/-! ## §3. Sections through a common point coincide -/

/-- **Two sections of a `k`-scheme through the same point coincide.** For a
scheme `X` over `Spec k` and sections `e₁, e₂` of the structure morphism with
`e₁(*) = e₂(*)`, already `e₁ = e₂`: the common image point is `k`-rational
(`bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section`), a morphism `Spec k ⟶ X` at a
fixed point is determined by its stalk data (`specToEquivOfLocalRingAt`), and
the stalk data of a section is a *local retraction* `𝒪_{X,x} → k` of the
structure homomorphism — unique at a rational point
(`IsLocalRing.ringHom_ext_of_surjective_residue_comp`). -/
theorem overSection_ext (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    {e₁ e₂ : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ X.left}
    (h₁ : e₁ ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (h₂ : e₂ ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (hbase : e₁.base default = e₂.base default) :
    e₁ = e₂ := by
  haveI : IsLocalRing ↥(CommRingCat.of k) := inferInstanceAs (IsLocalRing k)
  haveI : Subsingleton ↥(Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
===== 255,300
The representability leg proper. `pointedDualNumberPoints X e` below is the
functor-of-points tangent space: dual-number points of `X` over `Spec k` whose
closed point lands at `e(*)`. -/

/-- **Pointed dual-number points of `X` at `e`, over `Spec k`.** The
`k[ε]`-valued points of `X` lying over `Spec k[ε]` and landing at `e` — the
functor-of-points model of the Zariski tangent space `T_e X`. A named
restatement of the anonymous subtype the equivalences of
`Tangent/TangentIdentitySection.lean` target, kept for readability at the call
sites. -/
def pointedDualNumberPoints (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (e : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ X.left) :=
  {g : Spec (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k)) ⟶ X.left //
      g ≫ X.hom = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (DualNumber k)))
        ∧ g.base (closedPoint (DualNumber k)) = e.base default}

/-- **The tangent space of a represented functor, as a fibre.** Let `F` be a
functor on `Over (Spec k)` represented by a `k`-scheme `X`, and `e` a section of
the structure morphism. Composition with the representing natural bijection
identifies `T_e X` with the fibre of the restriction map
`F(Spec k[ε]) → F(Spec k)` (along the `ε ↦ 0` point) over the class of `e`. The
base-point condition transports to the fibre condition by
`specMap_fstRingHom_comp_eq` (sections through a common rational point
coincide). -/
noncomputable def pointedDualNumberPointsEquivRepresentableFiber
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    {F : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v}
    (rep : F.RepresentableBy X)
    {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ X.left}
    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
    pointedDualNumberPoints X e
      ≃ {a : F.obj (Opposite.op (overDualNumber k)) //
          F.map (overDualNumberZero k).op a
            = rep.homEquiv
                (Over.homMk e he : Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ⟶ X)} where
  toFun g :=
    ⟨rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.1 g.2.1 : overDualNumber k ⟶ X), by
      rw [← rep.homEquiv_comp]
      exact DFunLike.congr_arg rep.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext
        (specMap_fstRingHom_comp_eq X he g.2.1 g.2.2))⟩
  invFun a :=
    ⟨(rep.homEquiv.symm a.1).left,
      Over.w (rep.homEquiv.symm a.1),
      by
        haveI : Subsingleton ↥(Spec (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k))) :=
          inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum (DualNumber k)))
